title: Colour before the dark
caption: Sunset colours over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The setting Sun paints the sky over ESO's Paranal Observatory in pink, orange, purple, blue and yellow. The observatory sits high on top of a mountain in Chile, looking out over the Atacama Desert.

From that height, Paranal enjoys sweeping views of the desert around it. More important for astronomers, though, are the skies: clear and beautiful. A site like this is chosen for what happens after the colours fade.

The rainbow of hues comes from sunlight travelling through a long path of atmosphere when the Sun is low. Air scatters blue light more than red, so at sunset the light reaching us near the horizon is rich in warm colours, while higher up the sky still holds blues and purples. This short, colourful spell is a prelude: once it is over, the telescopes on the summit begin their night's work.

understand.eye: Sunset colours like these are visible to the eye, though a camera can record them with more saturation than a person may perceive.

explore: ESO's Paranal Observatory is home to the Very Large Telescope. ESO notes the sweeping desert views from the site, but the skies matter more. This colourful spell at sunset comes just before the dark hours in which the observatory's telescopes do their work.
